In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monolayers at the air-water interfaces at low pH are not stable enough to withstand the mineralization process.
the oscillation of the monolayer has a strong effect on the mineralization at low and high pH.
the oscillation of the polymer film at the air-water boundary leads to the formation of different mineralization products depending on the pH of the subphase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the monolayers at pH 5 and pH 8 are quite stable, but the mineralization products are quite different.
mechanical effects are important for mineralization at interfaces.
oscillations lead to a more uniform particle morphology, whereas at the same time the particle size is smaller and the mineralization rate is faster than in the case of a static monolayer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oscillating surface pressure leads to a more uniform mineralization product.
the oscillating monolayer is not a stable barrier against mineralization.
oscillation can lead to a change in the mineralization products and that these effects are strongly dependent on the pH of the subphase.
